thread:
tess.sre: Quick announcement + coordination: we're running a staggered maintenance + failover drill next Wed 03:30-05:00 UTC. Goal: validate cross-AZ failover paths and rebaseline serving SLOs after recent routing changes.

leo-sre: Which routes/pools are in scope?

tess.sre: Phase 1: control-plane DB read replicas (read-only switchover) in eu-west1, us-west1. Phase 2: serving pool failover for a small subset (svc-canary-2) to test cold-start behavior. No Dedicated customer pools.

anna-pm: We're also using this to finalize the new SLO target doc. Current proposal: p95 request latency = 120ms, p99 = 420ms for cold-start-sensitive routes. Note: p99 allowance increased to account for cold starts during failover.

max-platform: FYI autoscaler will be temporarily set to conservative mode during the drill to avoid noisy scaling. I'll apply: `redwoodctl autoscaler set --policy conservative --duration 90m`.

zeke-oncall: Oncall plan? I can be primary for the window.

tess.sre: Thanks. Zeke primary, Leo backup. Runbook snippet: 1) start maintenance: `redwoodctl maintenance start --id drill-1991123456 --stagger true` 2) monitor: serving.p99, controlplane.replica_lag, node.evictions 3) rollback: `redwoodctl maintenance abort --id drill-1991123456`. Full runbook in /docs/sre/drills.md.

maintenance-bot: Maintenance task "drill-1991123456" created -> Wed 1991123456T03:30:00Z. Notifications enabled for #eng-sre and oncall.

leo-sre: Can we add an alert suppression window for non-actionable noise? I hate alert storms during drills.

tess.sre: Yes — suppress non-critical alerts via `alertctl suppress --tag drill-1991123456 --until 1991123899`. Critical alerts (node.restarts, db.failover) will still fire.

anna-pm: Heads-up for product teams: no customer-visible rollouts during the window. I'll send a calendar invite and short note in #product.

max-platform: I'll pre-warm a small number of standby nodes in EU to reduce cold-start tail. Command: `infractl prewarm --pool eu-west1-standby --count 4`.

zeke-oncall: I'll arrive at 03:10 UTC and run a quick pre-check: controlplane replica lag < 100ms, all node-probes green.

(--- drill runs ---)

maintenance-bot: Maintenance "drill-1991123456" started (03:30 UTC). Phase: control-plane read-replica switchover.

leo-sre: Replica switchover complete in eu-west1. controlplane.replica_lag peaked at 230ms then recovered. No client errors observed.

tess.sre: Proceeding to Phase 2: triggered serving pool failover for svc-canary-2. Expect increased cold-starts for ~6 min while warmers spin up.

zeke-oncall: Observed serving.p99 spike to ~540ms for 7 minutes, p95 remained stable. No node.evictions.

anna-pm: Noted QoE impact. We'll record this for SLO analysis.

max-platform: Prewarm helped p99 tail reduced by ~30s of extreme spikes (see dashboard link in runbook).

maintenance-bot: Maintenance phase complete (04:12 UTC). Starting cleanup: autoscaler policy restore and alert suppression removal.

leo-sre: Post-run checks: all replicas healthy, node-probes green, no unexpected restarts.

tess.sre: Postmortem summary (short): - controlplane replica lag: transient peak 230ms - serving.p99: +28% for ~7m during failover - no customer routes degraded beyond internal canary - autoscaler behaved as expected. Full writeup scheduled in #eng-sre/postmortems.

anna-pm: Based on this, we propose updating the SLO doc to set p99 = 450ms for cold-start-sensitive routes and creating a separate cold-start budget. I'll draft and share for review.

zeke-oncall: Good drill. +1 for repeating monthly on a small scope.

maintenance-bot: Maintenance "drill-1991123456" closed (04:34 UTC). Post-run report attached.

max-platform: I'll follow up with exact numbers and cost delta.

leo-sre: Thanks team. Closing the loop: add a note in #engineering-all about the SLO tweak after Anna's doc is final.

tess.sre: Thanks everyone. Great coordination.
